chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Three months in Los Angeles at the Club Brazil
summary: They lived in Los Angeles while the club was in Chinatown, popular after Panchito Riset, and the show was broadcast.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: III - 129

Okay, fine. All right, so I notice that the picture that you showed me at the Club Brazil, 1946, the one that Bing Crosby is in and Lena Romay is in -- ahh - Rene is in that band with Julio Andino, Mangual, Uba Nieto and that - and I understand there was a live broadcast from the Club Brazil ....
Yes.
....most people heard here, because you showed me a record or something or a tape that Tango ....
"Tango Si - Rumba No," o"Rumba No" o"Rumba Si, Tango No"....
..."Rumba Si, Tango No"...
Yeah, yeah, that was .....
That was ....
....Marcelino Guerra number.
.... that was taped from a show in the Club Brazil in there. How long did you remain in Los Angeles?
Three months.
Three months. Where did you stay at out there?
Well, we were living in Los Angeles. The club was located in Chinatown and we used to live in Los Angeles.
What did you fellows do during the daytime for those three months that you were there? Do you remember?

Well, imagine! We were so popular, because that was the only thing that happened, I mean, in Cuban music or Latin music, in Los Angeles, because Panchito Riset was before and he created a good atmosphere up there, so when we
got there - Naturally we had -- our band was more, let's say more loud, because Panchito knew we had a good band, beautiful, he singing beautiful.
Panchito Riset was out there?

Yes, he was, con La Conga he went out there. As a matter of fact, when Panchito left to Los Angeles or to Hollywood, ahhh - La Rosa, is another Cuban band leader, he organized a band and he joined the first La Conga. That was in 57th and 5th Avenue; and Alfredito Valdes was the lead singer. I was the second voice and Oh!, we had a tremendous time. Alfredito Valdes, Vicentico Valdes's brother ...
Uh - Huh
.... we spent out there about three or four months.
